close_reason: Already-defended. task.rs:99-101 (and the sibling sites in task_list.rs / task_notification.rs) already carry the rationale: '// error). Without this, a /set against an unknown accountId would silently "succeed" with a fake oldState/newState envelope. Fixed in JMAP-gpt1.' The bead's defense ask — anchor the account_exists pre-check against future 'optimizing' contributors — is satisfied by the existing comment which both states the failure mode and cites the originating bead. No code change needed.
description: Each of task.rs:104-110, task_list.rs:62-68, task_notification.rs:62-68 calls backend.account_exists(caller, &account_id) immediately after extracting accountId and returns accountNotFound (RFC 8620 §3.6.2) before reading old_state or doing anything else. Without this, a /set call against an unknown accountId would proceed: get_state returns State::from('0') by default, the handler would produce a synthesized {oldState: '0', newState: '0', created: null, ...} envelope, and the caller would believe their request succeeded. A future contributor 'optimizing' this away ('account_exists is redundant if get_state checks the account') is wrong — get_state in the MemoryBackend has no such check (returns 0 for unknown accounts as a convenience for first-touch state). The check is structural, not optional. Same justification for the corresponding handler in jmap-mail-server/sibling extensions.
title: Defend: accountId-not-found early rejection (JMAP-gpt1) on all three /set handlers
